title: eSentire: Vinci RAT delivered through a Microsoft Store app called Setup Assistant after a fake snipping-tool download
date_note: eSentire's post, published 24 November, gives only that the intrusion began in early November 2026; the post's own day is used.
geo_basis: victim and location not stated in the sources
summary: eSentire's Threat Response Unit says it investigated an intrusion in early November 2026 that began when a victim searching for a snipping tool reached a fake download site. The site delivered a Microsoft-signed Store installer that installed an Electron app, Setup Assistant, published by "ETPS Ltd", which led to Vinci RAT, a PowerShell-based remote access trojan. eSentire says Microsoft stated, after its abuse report, that the app did not violate its terms.
plain: Researchers at eSentire say a fake snipping-tool site led a victim to install a Microsoft Store app that opened the way for a remote access trojan on a Windows PC.
exec: eSentire says an app listed in the Microsoft Store was used to deliver a remote access trojan, and that Microsoft stated it did not violate its terms.
action: eSentire advises restricting Microsoft Store installs using GPO, AppLocker, WDAC or Intune, and requiring security review before approving unknown or low-reputation apps.

validation.note: The findings come from eSentire's own research post; GBHackers relays it and is not independent. Microsoft's own statement was not read.

review.note: Setup Assistant, ETPS, Electron, PowerShell RAT, Microsoft reply, advice checked against eSentire
